Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
400 AM EDT Mon Sep 28 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Coastal Flood Advisories have been cancelled. Timing and
coverage of rain remains uncertain for the weekend.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Tranquil weather is expected through the middle of the week
  with climbing temperatures.

- 2) A cold front will approach on Friday, leading to cooler and
  potentially unsettled weather for the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Tranquil weather is expected through the middle
of the week with climbing temperatures.

The weakening Nor'easter is beginning to move away from the New
Jersey coast and will continue to progress northeastward today
as a blocking ridge to the north translates eastward. Before it
does so, a few light showers/patches of drizzle continue across
mainly north central and northeastern Maryland. It appears the
risk for rain will start declining by mid morning. Some CAM
reflectivity forecasts try to spit out a few sprinkles this
afternoon from the residual shallow moisture layer, but have
left the forecast dry for now. That moisture will result in
persistent clouds through the day, especially across the
northern half of the area. Clouds will hold temperatures in the
upper 60s to lower 70s, except mid 70s in central Virginia where
there may be more breaks of sun. Winds will be lighter than the
weekend as the pressure gradient relaxes.

Some clouds likely linger through tonight. Some fog may develop
west of the Blue Ridge, if there are breaks. Lows will largely
be in the 50s.

Ridging at the surface and aloft will build toward the eastern
US for the middle of the week, leading to a steady warming
trend. Residual moisture may remain trapped beneath the
subsidence inversion with weak gradients on Tuesday, although
deeper mixing will likely support more breaks of sun. While dry
conditions are most likely, it's worth noting some guidance
indicates there may be a brief shower or sprinkle as the
mid/upper level trough axis will still be overhead. Highs will
be closer to normal in the 70s.

Temperatures will climb further Wednesday and Thursday, with
more locations reaching the 80s. Some spots could even reach the
upper 80s by Thursday. Developing southerly flow will lead to
more sunshine. Dry weather is expected both days. With light 
winds and elevated dew points, some patchy fog could form during
the overnight hours.
 

KEY MESSAGE 2...A cold front will approach on Friday, leading to
cooler and potentially unsettled weather for the weekend.

Expect continued warm conditions Friday in response to the 
above average heights across the region. Unlike many ridges that
stagnate during the summertime, this feature is forecast to be 
more transient in nature while edging off the Atlantic coast by 
Friday. Amplifying flow in the northern stream will allow a 
longwave trough to graze the area by Friday into Saturday. Given
the height falls are rather weak, the accompanying cold front
which reaches the area on Friday likely stalls just off to the 
south through the weekend. The pattern turns a bit more 
unpredictable by Sunday into early next week. An elongated area 
of vorticity spinning initially around the Southern Plains may 
begin to edge northeastward in time. Enhanced vertical motions 
plus increasing moisture fluxes would support a risk for more 
concentrated rainfall. However, uncertainty is rather high given
the mesoscale nature of these features.

As the weak surface boundary nears the area, rain chances 
return to the forecast for Friday. Given the weak nature of the 
front and limited upper- level support, such chances are largely
capped around 20 to 40 percent. As mentioned above, this 
frontal system is likely to linger just off to the south for the
weekend. This will maintain a continued threat for rain along 
with cooler temperatures. At this point, daily highs are 
forecast to be in the 60s, with 50s at night given the abundant 
clouds and further rain chances.

&&

.AVIATION /07Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Ceilings are variable across the area as of 4 AM, but guidance
continues to forecast that MVFR ceilings will fill in for all
locations except CHO. A brief shower or some drizzle may also
affect BWI and MTN through sunrise. MVFR cigs will likely 
persist through mid-afternoon before improving back to VFR 
later in the afternoon. Northwest winds will generally remain
less than 10 kt.

Guidance suggests MVFR ceilings or some patchy fog if there are
breaks could develop at MRB overnight. Otherwise VFR conditions
are expected. 

High pressure will provide tranquil weather for Tuesday through
Thursday. The only potential impacts would be from early morning
fog (greatest chances at MRB and CHO).

As a cold front pushes through on Friday, some showers return, 
but restrictions look unlikely at this time. Initial winds will 
be southerly before shifting to west to northwesterly by Friday 
behind the cold front. Gusts up to 10 to 15 knots are possible 
as this boundary crosses through.

&&

.MARINE...
Winds have been decreasing this morning as the weakening
Nor'easter starts progressing northeastward away from the New
Jersey Coast. A couple zones of the Small Craft Advisory were
extended until 6 AM with residual channeled northwest flow. 
However, remaining advisory zones may be able to be cancelled 
prior to their 2 PM expiration.

High pressure moving toward the area will provide light winds
Tuesday and Wednesday. A northwesterly direction will turn
southerly on Wednesday.

Southerly winds begin to pick up in strength on Thursday, with some 
channeling effects bringing gusts to near 20 knots over the more 
southern waters. A cold front moves through on Friday which yields a 
shift to northerly flow. This comes with an uptick in post-frontal 
winds which may favor Small Craft Advisories for Friday evening into 
the night. 

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
The remaining Coastal Flood Advisories were cancelled as
water levels continue to decline. Some uncertainty exists for
the remainder of the week as guidance indicates anomalies will
stagnate close to 1 foot above normal. As long as it stays near
this value, most locations should remain below minor flood
thresholds. However, Annapolis could have minor flooding for
some tide cycles depending on how exactly the water levels
fluctuate.

&&
